html:
Sound system hire in Nairobi is easiest to get right when you match the equipment to three things: how many guests you expect, whether the event is indoors or outdoors, and whether the programme is mostly speech or mostly music. Add LED screens and stage lighting to that plan early, book a site survey, and leave enough time for setup and a proper sound check. This guide walks you through every decision, step by step.

Key takeaways

  • Size by guests and space: guest numbers, room size and indoor or outdoor setting decide how much PA system you need.
  • Speech and music need different setups: conferences need clarity and enough microphones; concerts and receptions need more bass and power.
  • Daylight changes the screen choice: LED screens stay visible in bright conditions where projectors struggle.
  • Power is part of the plan: confirm venue power and arrange a generator or backup where needed.
  • Timeline matters: survey, setup, sound check, show and pack down all need scheduled time.
  • Send full details: a complete brief gets you an accurate quote faster.

How big a sound system do I need for my event?

Start with your guest count, then adjust for the space. An indoor hall with walls and a ceiling holds sound well, so a modest system goes a long way. An open garden or field has nothing to reflect sound back, so you need more speakers, more power and often extra speakers further back so guests at the rear hear as clearly as those at the front. Tents sit in between: they block wind and some outside noise, but canvas does not hold sound like a solid room.

Speech or music: why it changes your PA system hire

A conference, AGM, graduation or church service is a speech event. The priority is clear, even sound across the whole audience, with no feedback and enough microphones for every speaker and panellist. Our conference & PA systems are planned around intelligibility first.

A wedding reception, concert, product launch or party is a music event. You need more low end from subwoofers, more headroom so the system is not straining, and inputs for a DJ, live band or playback laptop. Many events are both: speeches during the day and a dance floor at night. Tell us your full programme so the system covers every part of it.

Choosing microphones

Microphones are where many events go wrong. A few points to plan for:

  • Handheld wireless microphones suit MCs, speeches and Q&A sessions. Industry-standard vocal models such as the Shure SM58 and Beta 58A are popular because they are durable and handle loud voices well.
  • Lapel (lavalier) and headset microphones keep a presenter's hands free and work well for preachers, trainers and panel moderators.
  • Gooseneck microphones suit lecterns and head tables.
  • Instrument microphones and DI boxes are needed for live bands and choirs.

Count the people who will speak at the same time, not the total number of speakers. A panel of five needs five live microphones. Always ask for spare batteries and at least one backup microphone.

Do I need stage monitors?

Monitors are speakers that face the people on stage so they can hear themselves. Musicians, choirs and worship teams almost always need them. For a simple speech event, one monitor near the lectern helps the speaker pace themselves. Monitors must be placed and set carefully, because a badly positioned monitor is a common cause of feedback.

LED screen hire in Nairobi: LED wall or projector?

Screens let everyone see the speaker, slides, live camera feed or sponsor content. The main choice is between an LED wall and a projector with a screen.

  • Daytime and outdoor events: an LED screen produces its own light, so it stays readable in daylight. Outdoor-rated LED panels are far brighter than indoor ones and are built to handle the weather.
  • Tents and marquees: daylight passes through canvas and side openings, which washes out projection. LED is usually the safer choice unless the tent can be properly darkened.
  • Darkened halls and boardrooms: a projector can be a practical, cost-effective option where you control the lighting.

Screen size depends on how far back your audience sits. Tell us the depth of the seating area and we will recommend a size and position. See our LED screen services for more detail.

Stage lighting in Kenya: the basics

Good lighting makes people on stage visible to the audience and to cameras, and it sets the mood. The common fixtures are:

  • Wash lights: spread soft, even colour across the stage or a wall. They are the foundation of most designs.
  • Spot and profile lights: focus a defined beam on a speaker, couple or performer.
  • Moving heads: motorised fixtures that change position, colour and pattern, adding energy to concerts, launches and dance floors.
  • Haze: a light, even mist that makes beams visible in the air. Check with the venue first, because haze can set off some smoke detectors.
  • Uplighting: fixtures placed at floor level to colour walls, pillars, tent linings or trees. It is one of the most effective ways to transform a wedding venue in your colour theme.

Explore our lighting services to see how wash, spot and effects lighting come together.

Staging, truss and rigging

A raised stage improves sightlines and gives your speakers, band or bridal party a clear focal point. Truss is the aluminium framework used to hang lights, speakers and screens safely above the stage. For larger events, ground-supported truss allows a full lighting rig and LED screen without relying on the venue's ceiling. All rigging should be installed and checked by trained crew, and the stage should be level, stable and fitted with steps.

Power and generators

Sound, lighting and LED screens all draw significant power, and a power cut in the middle of vows or a keynote is the outcome everyone wants to avoid. Before booking, confirm:

  • Where the venue's power points are and how far they are from the stage.
  • Whether the venue supply can carry the full load, or whether a generator is needed.
  • Who provides fuel and who operates the generator.
  • Whether there is backup power for critical items such as the mixer and microphones.

Outdoor sites in particular often need a dedicated generator. We assess power needs during the site survey.

Event production timeline: from survey to pack down

  1. Enquiry and quote: you send your event details and we confirm availability and send a same-day quote.
  2. Site survey: for larger or outdoor events, we visit the venue to check layout, power, access and load-in routes.
  3. Setup: crew deliver and install equipment. Smaller setups take a few hours; large stages, screens and lighting rigs may need the day before.
  4. Sound check: microphones, playback, band and screen content are tested well before guests arrive.
  5. Show: our on-site technician runs or supports the system throughout the event.
  6. Pack down: equipment is dismantled and removed within the venue's allowed time.

Share the venue's access times early. Some venues only allow setup on the event day, which affects how much can be installed.

Why on-site technicians matter

Equipment is only as good as the person running it. A technician balances microphone levels as speakers change, controls feedback, cues music and walk-in tracks, and fixes problems quickly. Every VTECH hire package includes an on-site technician, so you are never left with a system and no one to operate it.

Contingency and backups

Professional event production in Kenya means planning for things going wrong. Ask your supplier about:

  • Spare microphones, batteries and cables on site.
  • A backup playback device for music and presentations.
  • Rain cover for outdoor equipment and a plan if the weather turns.
  • A clear contact person on both sides during the event.

Noise permits and venue rules

Kenya's noise regulations limit how loud events can be, depending on the area and time of day. Events using amplified sound that can be heard outside a building may need a noise permit from the relevant county government, so check this early, especially for outdoor and late-night events. Venues also set their own rules on sound limits, finishing times, haze, rigging and load-in. Confirm these with your venue and share them with us so the system is planned to comply.

What to send when requesting a quote

The more detail you give, the faster and more accurate your quote. Include:

  • Event date, start and finish times, and setup access times.
  • Venue name and location, and whether it is indoors, outdoors or in a tent.
  • Expected number of guests.
  • Type of event and programme: speeches, panels, DJ, live band, choir.
  • Number of microphones needed at the same time.
  • Whether you need an LED screen, projector, stage, truss or lighting.
  • Power availability and any venue restrictions.

Packages vs custom audio visual hire

Packages are the quickest route for common events. Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum are sized for up to 50, 150, 500 and 1,000 guests and include delivery, setup and an on-site technician. A custom quote suits events with a live band, multiple stages, large outdoor sites, broadcast or streaming needs, or audiences above 1,000. faqs.q: How far in advance should I book sound system hire in Nairobi?
faqs.a: Book as early as your date is confirmed, especially for weekends and the busy wedding and end-of-year seasons. Early booking secures equipment and crew, and leaves time for a site survey on larger or outdoor events. Last-minute requests are welcome, and VTECH will confirm availability and send a same-day quote.

faqs.q: Can I hire just a microphone or speaker without a full package?
faqs.a: Yes. If you only need a few items, such as wireless microphones, a pair of speakers or a projector, you can request individual equipment instead of a package. Tell us what you need, the date and the venue, and we will advise whether a technician or extra items would help your event run smoothly.

faqs.q: Do you provide sound and screens for events outside Nairobi?
faqs.a: Yes, we can support events outside Nairobi. Share the venue location, date and programme when you request a quote so we can plan transport, crew travel and setup time. For distant or outdoor venues, we may recommend a site survey or a detailed call to confirm power, access and layout first.

faqs.q: Can you livestream or record our conference or church service?
faqs.a: Audio visual setups can include a clean audio feed for recording or streaming, and camera feeds can be shown on screens in the venue. If you plan to livestream, mention it in your request so we can plan the right mixer outputs and connections, and coordinate with your streaming or video team.

faqs.q: What happens if equipment fails during my event?
faqs.a: Our on-site technician monitors the system throughout the event and carries spares such as microphones, batteries and cables to deal with common issues quickly. Planning backups for playback and power before the day reduces risk further. Discuss your critical moments, such as vows or keynotes, so we can protect them.
